request.spec:
A sheet id entry and a button compare this sheet with another: one line per grade of this sheet,
<grade> <this sheet's summary due-total for the grade> <the other sheet's>, 0.00 for a grade the
other sheet has no one on; a sheet that does not exist gives no lines.

agent.result_text:
You can now compare this sheet with another one. On the screen at `/` there's a sheet id box and a Compare button. They show one line per grade in the form `<grade> <this sheet's due-total> <the other sheet's>`. A grade the other sheet has no one on shows `0.00`, and a sheet id that has never been loaded shows no lines. All four tests in the spec pass, run through `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/exists`, says whether a sheet has been loaded. It's needed because the normal sheet requests create a sheet just by being asked for it. Without this check, comparing with an unknown id would quietly create that sheet and show `0.00` lines instead of nothing.
- **Front end:** the new `features/compare/SheetCompare.tsx` sits next to the summary in `PeopleList.tsx`. This sheet's numbers are the same per-grade due-totals the summary shows: people retired today are left out and `n/a` counts as nothing. The other sheet's numbers are worked out the same way, using the same figure code the consolidated view uses for other sheets. The lines clear on each press and come back only once the other sheet's data has finished loading, so you never see half-loaded numbers.

**Port clash on this machine:** my first run, on the default port 3000, failed in "scenario 2". That test never uses the compare feature; it failed on the order of a person's claims after a merge. Other sandboxes are running their own copies of the app on ports 3000–3003, so I believe that run raced with one of theirs. My follow-up reruns definitely hit someone else's server, because mine hadn't started. I didn't confirm the cause, but the full suite passed on a private port with `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`. If you see that failure again, run on a free port.
